name: Ixcatec
confidence_why: Adamou, Gordon & Gries 2018 place Ixcatec stress on the penultimate syllable of the root alongside its three tones, but that placement comes from an unpublished 2012 talk by DiCanio, Adamou herself wrote in 2014 and again in 2019 that whether Ixcatec has stress at all is still under discussion, and the only phonological description, Fernández Carrillo 1950, treats prominence as predictable from tone rather than as independent stress.

catalog_quote: Ixcatec has three tones that contrast in word-final syllables: high (H), mid (M), and low (L). In non-final syllables, the contrast between mid and low tone is neutralized in favor of the mid tone (see DiCanio 2011 for a preliminary phonetic analysis of Ixcatec tone). Stress in Ixcatec typically falls on the penultimate syllable and is associated with increased duration and intensity and higher F0 (DiCanio 2012). ... unstressed vowels in Ixcatec typically have reduced duration, intensity and F0 relative to their stressed counterparts (DiCanio 2012). ... It should be noted that the coding for the variable STRESS was the same in the suffixed as in the unsuffixed forms since the suffix falls outside the domain of stress and thus does not trigger a rightward shift of stress from the penultimate syllable of the root. tone_statements.quote: Popoloc, Chocho, and Ixcatec have three contrastive level tones, which are present in both the lexicon and the grammar: High (H), Mid (M), and Low (L) (for Popoloc see Veerman-Leichsenring 1991, for Chocho see Veerman-Leichsenring 2000a, for Ixcatec see Fernández de Miranda 1959). The pitch tracks for two minimal pairs from Ixcatec are presented in Figures 3a, 3b and 4a, 4b where it can be see that the low tone is realized as a falling tone; we also note that the low tone is realized only utterance-finally and neutralized utterance-medially as a mid tone.

tone_statements.quote: In Ixcatec (Popolocan), low tones surface only at the end of a phonological phrase. In phrase-internal (but word-final) position, all low tones neutralize with mid tone (DiCanio, submitted). In the left panel of Figure 1, we observe complete overlap in the production of low and mid tones. These same target words are realized with different tones when they appear in utterance-final position.

Como es una lengua tonal, Alarcón supone que la tonía no se utiliza como correlato fonético para esta lengua y sugiere que son la duración y la intensidad las pistas acústicas de la prominencia. ... El autor también sugiere que de los tres tonos, bajo, medio y alto, el bajo es más inestable.
tone_statements.translation: Finally, Rafael Alarcón's paper 'Phonetic correlates of stress in Ixcatec' presents the phonetic correlates of stress in Ixcatec, a Popolocan language of the Otomanguean stock. Since it is a tonal language, Alarcón assumes that pitch is not used as a phonetic correlate in this language and suggests that duration and intensity are the acoustic cues of prominence. ... The author also suggests that of the three tones, low, mid and high, the low one is the most unstable.
